- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast by 2–5% for consecutive high sentiment days.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (forecast peaks > 75% above recent mean) — adjust downward by 10–15% if sentiment drops below 0.3.
- Lagged overreaction: if forecast is high 3–5 days after a spike, reduce by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is consistently above 72–74 for 3+ consecutive days, cap at 72.5 and reduce slope.
- Sentiment reversal triggers: if sentiment drops below 0.2 after 3+ days of high sentiment, cut forecast by 5–8% and shift to downward trend.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts overestimate early in low sentiment cycles — reduce first 5–7 days by 3–5% if sentiment < 0.3.
- Avoid “sentiment echo”: if sentiment is high but price drops, don’t overcorrect — reduce forecast only if true drop > 5% from prior peak.
